sentences.text: Thus, the plaintiff and defendants no.1 to 7 are at common ground regarding the suit properties belonging to Sirilal.
From the material on record, it can be ascertained that the suit properties are Birmati Vs. Suraj Bhan & Ors.
Pages 17 of 23 self-acquired properties of Sirilal.
The question which now arises is whether he died intestate or left Will dated 30.05.1995?
Accordingly, how would the property devolve upon the legal heirs?
25. Defendants no.1 to 7 have relied upon Will tendered as Ex.DW1/1.
However, the Will was not proved.
No attesting witness in view of Section 68 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 were examined.
Therefore, the Will which is not admitted by the plaintiff being unproved, is inadmissible in evidence and there is no basis on which, this Court can hold that Sirilal died intestate.
Therefore, the devolution of his estate of Sirilal would be as per Hindu Succession Act, 1956.
It is for this reason that the Court is of the view that the controversy of date of death of Sirilal and authenticity of rival death certificates are no longer relevant.

26. It has been sought to be shown by the defendants that a family arrangement was put in place by giving the plaintiff a plot of land at Village Goyala to settle her claims against the estate of Sirilal during the lifetime of Sirilal.

However, during cross-examination of the plaintiff on 21.05.2009,
defendants no.1 & 2 only suggested that the aforesaid plot of land which was given to the plaintiff was only "in lieu of your entire share in his land?" and the same was denied.
It was not suggested to the witness that it was also in lieu of other properties of Sirilal.
She also deposed that it was only out of threat and terror that Sirilal share the rental income only with her brothers.
DW-2 Sh. Digamber is another witness examined to shed light on the family Birmati Vs. Suraj Bhan & Ors.
Pages 18 of 23 arrangement.
However, he was traversed on his deposition of intention of Sirilal of bequeathing of his properties to his grandsons and his awareness of the properties of Sirilal.
From his cross-examination it also appears that in the year 1992-93, itself, Sirilal had "Willed out his property" whereas, the Will relied upon by the defendants is of the year 1995.

Defendant no.4 when examined as DW3/W1 deposed that partition between family members had taken place on 04.10.1991 but during cross-examination stated that it referred to the partition between Sirilal and his brother.
He could not establish any partition after the death of Sirilal.
The cross-examination of defendant no.6 (D3W2) also shows that no partition between the heirs of Sirilal had been effected pursuant to his death.
27. One controversy which may crop up is qua the site plans and identities of the suit properties as there is some discrepancy qua Khasra number which defendant no.1 & 2 seek to rely upon.
